reviews.title: No Kanji
reviews.text:
This app really needs to incorporate kanji into Japanese learning. Teaching everything primarily in hiragana makes reading real Japanese more difficult, because Japanese is normally written using a combination of kanji, hiragana, and katakana.

A simple improvement would be to replace appropriate hiragana words with their standard kanji and provide furigana above the kanji for learners who still need help with pronunciation. This would allow users to learn how Japanese is actually written while still being able to read unfamiliar kanji.

Without enough kanji exposure, I feel like I’m learning to read Japanese in a way that doesn’t reflect what I actually encounter in Japan. Adding kanji with furigana would make the app significantly more useful for serious Japanese learners.

reviews.title: Best language app
reviews.text:
This is by far the best language app I’ve ever tried. It doesn’t use ai (to my knowledge), it’s basically free, and it has lessons that actually work in tons of languages! My only criticism is that you should add chapters on how to learn the different writing systems, and also to maybe add Esperanto. Thank you!
-an aspiring hyperpolyglot

reviews.title: Love to Vietnamese!
reviews.text: I normally never write a review for an app, but I am especially inspired today to express my appreciation for this app.  I have always wanted to improve my Vietnamese (my family speaks)but have always found it so difficult across various apps because of different pronunciations and the exaggerated formality of the language. As a speaker seeking to increase her vocabulary outside of a household setting, I commend your dedication to the language and the curriculum to actually teaching someone a language with the goal to put it to real world use with REAL conversation. My only complaint in the way the app is formatted. I think your mission is amazing but if the app was a little easier to navigate take Duolingo as inspiration maybe? Also vocabulary wise I am already familiar with many words as is but would love to add a unit one vocab word to a bigger vocab flash card list with more advanced words. Thank you MANGO team!

reviews.title: Just one bug to fix!
reviews.text: I remember hearing about Mango Languages 20 years ago and how it was potentially free if you did it at the library. I always wanted to try it, and now that we live in an age of smartphones where we can connect our apps to our library cards, this really is a great gift. I am one of those who completely lost faith in Duolingo once I realized that its business model relied on drip feeding people the feeling of education for as long as possible to keep getting their money rather than actually educating them. I am thrilled that this app exists, and I am thrilled that the institution of the library still exists in these dark times for public infrastructure so I need to give all of that prepuce before I register my one complaint: I have just started a French course and want to take advantage of the autoplay feature while I get ready in the morning, drive my car, etc. but unpredictably it will jump at seemingly random points in seemingly random exercises, skipping to the next. I don't want to miss any content because it was surely laid out with the repetitions by design. But I also don't want to have to sit beside it like a babysitter to advance slide after slide when there are so many opportunities throughout the day to let it just play to me. This one but being ironed out would make the app perfect for me.

reviews.title: Not good for Vietnamese
reviews.text:

Little did I know that they only have one unit for Vietnamese, and it was very much focused on tourist interactions (while also being way too advanced for a tourist lol)… and it definitely didn’t have any units with southern Vietnamese language used.

Oh well.

reviews.title: Meh
reviews.text: I have their paid subscription but am looking for alternatives to Duolingo because their predatory business model of constantly pushing PAID users to buy points for real money to buy your way through the levels really ruins the joy of learning a language for me. However, there seems to be no app that does it all perfectly. I find this app from the sample content to be very “dry” but two definite pluses are how the app explains WHY a phrase is said a certain way - it gives insight in to the literal meaning of a phrase- and in addition to speaking with a quality voice, it also shows the phonetic spelling to help you understand how to pronounce a word better. What I really don’t like is the push to sign up for an account- free or not- especially when it only lets me see a few basic words I already know. I want to know what other lessons and activities are contained in this app before even signing up; I have ZERO interest in signing up for yet another subscription trial. I want to know exactly what the content is ahead of time and THEN if it has value I will pay for it.

reviews.title: Paywall

For example, making the throaty Dutch sounds, or how to move your tongue to make certain sounds in Spanish, etc.

reviews.title: “How old are you” is incorrect in Japanese
reviews.text: I’m learning Japanese and the app taught me to say that “お歳は？ (otoshi wa)” is the correct way to ask how old are you. However, native speakers say that’s unnatural. The natural and polite way to ask is actually おいくつですか？ (oikutsu desu ka) and the informal way to say it would’ve been “何歳ですか” (nansai desu ka) so I’m kinda disappointed that Mango didn’t catch that

reviews.title: Still no Dark Mode and no Kanji
reviews.text:
There’s only “night mode” when doing a lesson but not when navigating the app or using flash cards. Please add an app-wide dark mode. 

One of the languages I’m learning is Japanese, I’d really like to see more Kanji being used in the lessons. Kanji is as important to Japanese as Hanzi (Chinese characters) is for Chinese. Mango manages to use Hanzi for Chinese immediately. Please fully incorporate Kanji in Japanese lessons—like is done for Chinese with the Hanzi characters.

reviews.title: Best language learning app
reviews.text:
This app has many advantages over others:

1. It reviews sentences, words, and grammar in context and teaches the words behind each phrase so that you don’t have to guess how to apply the words in a novel situation. 
2. It actually explains grammar and cultural elements. 
3. Repetition helps you learn. 
4. Huge range of languages!
5. It’s free through a lot of public libraries!

Go Mango!

reviews.title: Can you really learn German from an app?
reviews.text: Can you really learn another language like German from an app?  Well, yes and no.  I have now spent just shy of 25 months (961 hrs) learning German with Mango.  After a year I enrolled in a 1st semester German class at the local CC and I was very well prepared for it.  In fact, there was very little I hadn’t already seen until we were about 3/4 th through the semester.  You will have some gaps in grammar, but you will have plenty of practice actually speaking and pronouncing German.  Highly recommend!

reviews.title: Still has bugs
reviews.text:
I live in Germany, but I am not fluent in German. My husband is more fluent than I am and he greatly disliked the pre-test. I have not used this app in a while. After seeing the pre-test I’m wondering if updating the app was a good decision. The pre-test was weird. It was asking questions but not in the same way a normal German person would speak and even English speakers would not ask those same questions in that way. I also don’t like that every time you click a word all the words are scrambled. Maybe that’s cute for children, but not so great for me and my spouse. One of the frustrating things was the words we were looking for were not always present, or one tense of the word was there, but not the tense we wanted to use. Questions were answered wrong because the correct word was not present. For example a word we used was incorrect because it had an “s” at the end, but the correct spelling of the word we wanted was not present at the time of submission. I did not see a way to report errors in the pre-test. I am going to ask my German neighbor what she thinks to determine if using this program will be worth our time. 
Are people designing this program or is it Ai? That could potentially explain errors.

reviews.title: (Japanese) Useful Language Lessons
reviews.text: A lot of the lessons I have done over a few years on Mango appear to have a heavy focus on useful language, and there are also several grammar and cultural notes that I appreciate during lessons. However, it does not focus at all on Kanji (adapted Chinese characters) for Japanese, having only a few minor notes, mostly using kana (the phonetic alphabet scripts of Japanese). Additionally, it primary tone for the language it teaches is middle-level formal (not business, not casual), which is great for consistency in some ways, but leaves a lot to be desired. As a result of these short comings, I have had to supplement with other learning material, namely Kanji, casual Japanese, and language exchange apps. I also have some minor gripes about the Listen and Read sections at the end of each Chapter of lessons, namely that they introduce new vocabulary at the end of the chapter (when you should be applying learned information, not learning new information). This new vocabulary is also in list-form with no practice aids beyond what could be found in a dictionary (spelling and pronunciation). For context, when new vocabulary is introduced in a typical lesson, you would see, hear, and say it several times through guided practice as part of the lesson prior to and after the word or phrase is introduced, in addition to having spaced repetition practice for lesson sentences that include the vocabulary. The new words in the Listen and Read sections do none of that, just barely the dictionary information, although in the provided passage they are at least highlighted. I feel it would be better if those lists were in their own lesson prior to these sections. Overall, I like Mango, but its far from a stand-alone language learning app (many aren’t anyways). I just have those few complaints about content and structure I mentioned above.
